statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 12 sits in the low band while Stress 52 sits in the elevated band.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold. The 13:30-16:00 UTC span covering the US cash open and the Dallas Fed release is flagged as the window where conditional risk peaks; the mapped state stays EA_ON across the published horizon.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a fourth hour inside an unchanged 271-point overnight range into the US cash open as Brent eases to $90.52 and gold trades lower
body: Nasdaq-100 futures trade near 29,421.25, down about 0.24%, inside a day range of 29,274.75-29,545.50 that is now unchanged across four consecutive hourly assessments. Neither extreme has been retested and price sits in the lower half of the range. The overnight driver is unchanged: US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island near the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, breaking up an attempted mining operation, and Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they fired on US bases in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates. Kharg Island, handling roughly 90% of Iran's crude exports, has been publicly threatened and secondary sanctions on Iran's trading partners have been flagged. The important change since the previous assessment is that the energy premium is decaying rather than extending: Brent is near $90.52, up about 2.75%, against $91.04 reported earlier this morning, and WTI is near $85.53, up about 2.55%. Gold at about $4,495 is down roughly 0.77%, which is inconsistent with a one-way geopolitical risk-off path, and bitcoin is down about 1.08%. The 10-year Treasury yield is near 4.75%, up about 3.2 basis points, while the 2-year is near 4.35%, down marginally, a modest steepening rather than a yield shock. VIX is 15.34 with a 14.89-15.41 day range, up about 6.3% from Friday's 14.43 close but low in absolute terms. Index futures are only modestly lower, with S&P 500 E-minis down about 0.22% and Nasdaq-100 E-minis down about 0.14% in the late pre-market. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks have lifted September rate-hike odds to roughly 57-62% from about 41% a week earlier, and the Nasdaq-100 cash index closed Friday at 29,433.43. Today is the last trading session of August, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite tracking their first monthly gains since May, so month-end rebalancing is an additional mechanical factor into the 20:00 UTC close. Apple's long-announced leadership transition also lands at this month boundary, with Tim Cook's final day as chief executive today and John Ternus taking over on September 1; the succession was announced in April 2026 and is orderly rather than a shock. The decisive observation for this assessment is that a fourth full hour has passed with both range extremes rejected and neither retested, while oil has begun to give back part of its move and gold has fallen. That combination is direct evidence that mean reversion is functioning and that cross-assets conflict rather than align. The amplifier count remains meaningful but observed price-path structure stays two-sided, so the elevated event backdrop is carried in Stress rather than Tail. The US cash open occurs at the assessment cutoff, so no post-open structure has been observed; it is treated as a checkpoint, not as evidence. The Dallas Fed Manufacturing Index at 14:30 UTC has not yet been released and is carried as a scheduled checkpoint. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was about 344 minutes old at assessment time and was therefore treated as stale under the inherited freshness rule and excluded from the evidence base; every level above comes from independent primary-source research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments were available and every one mapped to EA_ON. Tail held at 5 through the Sunday reopen window, rose to 15 at 00:00 UTC as the Iran escalation was first priced, decayed back to 5 by 07:00-08:00 UTC, jumped to a peak of 17 at 09:00 UTC as oil extended, then eased through 11, 10 and 9 over the following three hours. Stress climbed from 26 to a peak of 52 and has drifted to 47. Dominant mode moved from normal to mixed after 23:00 UTC, with one trend-down hour at 00:00 UTC and event/whipsaw at 09:00 and 10:00 UTC. The shape of the window is an event shock that was absorbed rather than extended.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook keeps the mapped state at EA_ON for all 24 hours. Conditional Tail runs 12 in the current hour, peaks at 18 and 17 for the two hours inside the flagged 13:30-16:00 UTC window covering the cash open and the Dallas Fed release, then steps down to 11-14 through the US afternoon and rises to 15 for the 20:00 UTC month-end close. It settles to an 8-9 overnight baseline across the Asian session before drifting up to 10-14 through the European session as the September 1 ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS block at 14:00 UTC approaches from just beyond the horizon. Stress peaks near 56 around the cash open and decays toward 38-40 overnight. Confidence declines from 85 to 60 with horizon.
